## Introduction & Recruitment Overview

The Railway Recruitment Board Non-Technical Popular Categories (**RRB NTPC**) examination is one of India's largest competitive recruitment drives, attracting over 1.25 Crore aspirants competing for prestigious central railway positions. Administered across 21 regional RRBs under the Ministry of Railways, RRB NTPC selects candidates for both **Graduate Level (Pay Level 4, 5, and 6)** and **Undergraduate Level (Pay Level 2 and 3)** posts.

From vital train operations like **Goods Train Manager** and **Station Master** to central administrative positions like **Senior Commercial cum Ticket Clerk**, **Junior Accounts Assistant**, and **Chief Commercial cum Ticket Supervisor**, RRB NTPC offers long-term job security, comprehensive Railway Medical benefits (covering full family at Railway Central Hospitals), free privilege travel passes across India, and 7th Central Pay Commission compensation.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> **Unified Syllabus for CBT-1**: The preliminary screening test (CBT-1) is identical for both Graduate and Undergraduate categories. However, in CBT-2, separate computer-based tests are conducted for each 7th CPC Pay Level (Level 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6). High scores in CBT-1 are essential to clear the cutoff for multiple pay levels!

## Multi-Stage Selection Architecture

1. **First Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-1)**: Common screening examination for all posts to shortlist candidates at 15 times the vacancy count for CBT-2.
2. **Second Stage Computer Based Test (CBT-2)**: Separate merit-deciding examination conducted for each Pay Level (Level 2, 3, 5, and 6).
3. **Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)**: Applicable exclusively for **Station Master** candidates (Testing psychometric intelligence, spatial memory, and directional reaction speed).
4. **Typing Skill Test (TST)**: Mandatory qualifying test for Senior Clerk cum Typist, Junior Accounts Assistant, and Junior Clerk (30 WPM English or 25 WPM Hindi without spellcheck).
5. **Document Verification (DV) & Biometric Matching**: Strict verification of educational certificates, OBC-NCL / EWS certificates, and identity.
6. **Comprehensive Railway Medical Examination**: Strict vision standards (A-2 standard for Station Master and Goods Guard requiring 6/9 distant vision without glasses; fogging test applicable).

## CBT-1 Examination Pattern & Subject Weightage

CBT-1 is a 90-minute online test comprising 100 multiple-choice questions for 100 marks. Each wrong answer incurs a penalty of **1/3rd (0.33) marks**.

| Subject / Domain | Questions | Marks | Mark Weightage Graph | Sectional Focus Areas |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **General Awareness (GA)** | 40 Questions | 40 Marks | [BAR:40%:General Awareness] | Science (PCB up to 10th), Current Affairs, History, Geography, Polity, Static GK |
| **Mathematics (Quantitative Aptitude)** | 30 Questions | 30 Marks | [BAR:30%:Mathematics] | Arithmetic (Percentage, Ratio, SI/CI, Profit & Loss), Number Systems, Mensuration |
| **General Intelligence & Reasoning** | 30 Questions | 30 Marks | [BAR:30%:Reasoning] | Coding-Decoding, Series, Syllogisms, Blood Relations, Analogies, Puzzles |
| **Total Composite Test** | **100 Questions** | **100 Marks** | **[BAR:100%:Total Test]** | **Composite Time: 90 Minutes (120 Minutes for PwBD)** |

## CBT-2 Examination Pattern (Merit Deciding Stage)

CBT-2 is conducted for shortlisted candidates with higher difficulty level and 120 questions to be solved in the same 90-minute window.

| Subject / Domain | Questions | Marks | Mark Weightage Graph | Level of Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **General Awareness (GA)** | 50 Questions | 50 Marks | [BAR:41.7%:General Awareness] | High depth: Current scientific developments, Indian Constitution, Economic trends |
| **Mathematics (Quantitative Aptitude)** | 35 Questions | 35 Marks | [BAR:29.2%:Mathematics] | Advanced arithmetic, algebra, trigonometry, geometry, and data interpretation |
| **General Intelligence & Reasoning** | 35 Questions | 35 Marks | [BAR:29.2%:Reasoning] | Multi-variable puzzles, critical statements & assumptions, seating arrangements |
| **Total Composite Test** | **120 Questions** | **120 Marks** | **[BAR:100%:Total Test]** | **Duration: 90 Minutes (Negative Marking: 1/3rd mark)** |

## Granular Topic-Wise Syllabus Breakdown

### 1. Mathematics Syllabus (Complete Topic Index)
- **Number System & Simplification**: Fractions, Decimals, Surds & Indices, VBODMAS rules, Square Roots.
- **LCM & HCF**: Real-world application problems and divisible factors.
- **Ratio, Proportion & Variation**: Direct/inverse proportion, partnerships, ages.
- **Percentage, Profit & Loss**: Successive discounts, marked price, cheating dealer problems.
- **Simple & Compound Interest**: Half-yearly/quarterly compounding, difference between CI and SI.
- **Time, Speed, Distance & Trains**: Relative speed, boat & stream, circular tracks, train passing platforms.
- **Time & Work / Pipes & Cisterns**: Efficiency ratios, alternate work days, leak problems.
- **Mensuration (2D & 3D)**: Areas, perimeters, surface area, and volumes of cylinders, cones, and spheres.
- **Elementary Algebra**: Polynomials, linear equations in two variables, quadratic identities.
- **Geometry & Trigonometry**: Circles, tangents, triangles similarity, height & distance, standard trigonometric identities.
- **Elementary Statistics**: Mean, median, mode, standard deviation, and graphical representation.

### 2. General Intelligence & Reasoning Syllabus
- **Verbal Logic**: Analogies, Alphabetical & Number Series, Coding-Decoding (Letter shifting, Matrix).
- **Mathematical Operations**: Symbol substitution, equation balance.
- **Relationships & Family Tree**: Coded blood relations, pointing to photograph questions.
- **Analytical Reasoning**: Syllogisms (Venn diagram approach), Statement-Conclusion, Statement-Assumptions, Cause & Effect.
- **Arrangements & Puzzles**: Linear and circular seating arrangements, floor puzzles, scheduling.
- **Data Sufficiency**: Determining minimum statements required to answer.
- **Visual & Non-Verbal**: Paper folding/cutting, embedded figures, mirror & water images, dice & cubes.

### 3. General Awareness Syllabus (High-Scoring Section)
- **General Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology)**: 10th CBSE NCERT level; human circulatory/nervous systems, chemical reactions, periodic table, optics, mechanics, electricity.
- **Current Affairs of National & International Importance**: Last 12 months summits, appointments, sporting events, Padma/Gallantry awards, Nobel prizes, government welfare schemes.
- **Indian History & Freedom Struggle**: Ancient kingdoms, Delhi Sultanate, Mughal era, 1857 revolt, Gandhian movements, key constitutional acts.
- **Indian Polity & Constitution**: Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles, President, Parliament powers, Supreme Court, constitutional amendments.
- **Physical & Economic Geography**: River systems of India, mountain passes, national parks, mineral belts, agricultural seasons (Kharif/Rabi).
- **Indian Railways GK**: History of Indian Railways, Vande Bharat/bullet train corridors, railway zones and headquarters.
- **Computers & Information Technology**: Input/output devices, RAM/ROM, operating systems, MS Office shortcuts, Internet protocols, cybersecurity terms.

## High-Impact 90-Day RRB NTPC Study Plan

- **Days 1 to 30 (Foundation & NCERT Science)**: Master basic arithmetic calculation speeds (vedic math tables up to 30, squares up to 50, cubes up to 30). Read Class 9 & 10 NCERT Science thoroughly.
- **Days 31 to 60 (Sectional Drills & Puzzles)**: Solve 50 reasoning puzzles (linear & circular seating). Practice previous years' NTPC arithmetic questions. Memorize last 8 months of current affairs.
- **Days 61 to 75 (Full Mock Tests & Error Journal)**: Take one full-length CBT-1 mock test every alternate morning. Analyze every wrong question in an Error Notebook.
- **Days 76 to 90 (Speed Optimization & Negative Mark Control)**: Eliminate guesswork. Aim for 85+ attempts with 95% accuracy to secure maximum normalization benefit.
